The site describes the lessons as short and accessible and written for young readers.

records.title: Forgiveness in the Munajat Sha'baniyyah
records.description: A journal paper on the idea of forgiveness in the Munajat Sha'baniyyah, a whispered prayer (munajat) linked to the month of Sha'ban. Sections discuss ways of seeking pardon, acceptance of an apology and why people accept apologies.

records.title: The Formation of the Jaʿfari Shiʿa Islamic School of Law from its Inception to the Occultation
records.description: A footnoted article on the history of how the Jaʿfari school (the Shia school of Islamic law) developed from the time of Imam al-Sadiq and the other Imams until the Occultation. Its sections are an introduction and the period of the Imams.

records.title: Fortitude, the Bridge to Victory

records.title: Forty Hadith, An Exposition
records.description: A detailed commentary on forty selected traditions of the Prophet and his Ahl al-Bayt, mostly on ethics and spiritual self-improvement (self-struggle, showing off, pride, envy, anger and similar). The Persian original is said to date from 1939; Ansariyan Publications, Qum.

records.title: Al-Amālī: The Dictations
records.description: A transcription of 42 assemblies in which Shaykh al-Mufid dictated narrations to his students, shown with an English translation by Mulla Asgharali M M Jaffer. The site says it holds 387 narrations attributed to the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt (the Prophet's family) on historical, ethical and doctrinal topics. Its assemblies cover topics such as the recording of good deeds, the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt, supplications at dawn and dusk, the great sins, Ramadan and the fear of Allah. It is a primary source for readers with some background.

records.title: Al-Amālī: The Dictations
records.description: A transcription of 97 assemblies in which Shaykh al-Saduq dictated narrations to his students, shown with an English translation by Bilal Muhammad. Each assembly is dated by the day and month when it was held; the first assemblies are dated Rajab and Sha'ban. The site says it holds 1082 narrations attributed to the Prophet and the Ahl al-Bayt (the Prophet's family), including topics such as the Night Journey and Ascension, supplications and the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt. It is a primary source.

records.title: Al-Kāfi (Vol. 8): The Sufficient
records.description: Al-Kafi is a collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) compiled by Shaykh al-Kulayni, shown here in Arabic with an English translation by Muhammad Sarwar. Volume 8 of 8, called al-Rawda (the Garden), is a miscellaneous collection that the site says includes long narrations from letters and wills of the Imams and historical reports, not arranged by topic. Its 596 short chapters touch on many subjects, such as asceticism (zuhd), the Day of Judgment, dreams and the worthlessness of worldly life. It is a primary source, best suited to readers with some background.

records.title: Al-Tawḥīd: The Book of Divine Unity
records.description: A collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) about God, compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq and translated into English by Sayed Ali Raza Rizvi. Its chapters cover God's names and attributes, God's knowledge, will, power and speech, the nature of the Quran, free will and predestination, divine justice and guidance, and arguments against atheists and dualists. It is a primary source for readers who want the narrations behind Shia beliefs about God.

records.description: A work by Shaykh al-Saduq on the occultation (ghayba, meaning being hidden from view) of the twelfth Imam, Muhammad al-Mahdi, and on the Imamate, shown with an English translation by Sayyid Athar Husain S. H. Rizvi. Its first section covers the author's introduction, the necessity of the Imamate and the Imam's infallibility. The second section, 'The Occultations and the Proofs', begins with accounts of earlier prophets who were hidden for periods, such as Idris and Yusuf. It is a primary source for readers with some background.

records.description: A collection of narrations about ziyara, the practice of visiting sacred sites of the Shia, compiled by Ibn Qulawayh al-Qummi and shown in Arabic with an English translation by Sayyid Mohsen Al-Husayni Al-Milani. Its chapters cover the rewards for visiting the Prophet, Imam Ali, Hamzah and other holy persons, the merits of praying in the mosque of Kufah, the rewards for visiting graves, the Euphrates river, and the farewell said after a visit. It is a primary source rather than an introduction.

records.title: Kitāb al-Ḍuʿafāʾ: The Weakened Ones
records.description: A biographical reference on narrators of Shia hadith and their reliability, shown with an English translation by Tashayyu. The site says it is organised alphabetically and is also known as 'Rijal Ibn al-Ghada'iri' (rijal means the study of narrators). Its chapters are grouped by the first letter of each narrator's name, from Alif to Ya, with one chapter on kunyas (names that begin with Abu) and an addendum of material quoted from other authors. It is not a hadith collection; it is a tool for studying who transmitted hadith.

records.title: Kitāb al-Ghayba: The Book of Occultation
records.description: A book by Shaykh al-Nu'mani on the occultation (ghayba, meaning being hidden from view) of the twelfth Imam, shown in Arabic with an English translation by Abdullah al-Shahin. It has about 478 narrations in twenty-six chapters. Its chapters cover the Imamate and the twelve Imams, pretenders to the Imamate, patience and doubt during the occultation, the signs before the reappearance of al-Qa'im (the awaited Imam), the Sufyani, and the Imam's age. It is a primary source.
sample_questions: Who is the Mahdi?
What is the occultation of the twelfth Imam?
What are the signs of the Mahdi's reappearance?
Who was Shaykh al-Nu'mani?
What hadith are there about the twelve Imams?
What does the book say about pretenders to the Imamate?

H. Rizvi. It is a detailed primary source for readers with some background.

records.description: A collection of nearly three hundred narrations on ethics, character and zuhd (asceticism, meaning self-discipline and detachment from worldly things), compiled by al-Husayn b. Sa'id al-Ahwazi and shown with an English translation by Shaykh Tahir Ridha Jaffer. Its chapters cover silence and good speech, good character and anger, kindness to parents and relatives, the rights of neighbours, this world, humility and arrogance, showing off, repentance, death and the grave, and paradise and hell. It is a primary source for readers with some background.

records.description: A hadith collection (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) about Imam al-Rida, compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq and shown with an English translation by Dr. Ali Peiravi. Volume 2 of 2 includes the Imam's explanations of the reasons behind various things, his debates with opponents on divine leadership, his knowledge and insight, his martyrdom, and the reward of visiting his shrine. It is a primary source for readers with some background.
